skills.name: direction-expander
skills.purpose: Expand a one-line fiction direction into genre, protagonist, central conflict, selling points, payoff, reader expectations, and commercial tags.
skills.when_to_use: At the start of an outline, pitch, world, plot, or writing task when the user gives only a premise or vague direction.
skills.instructions: Identify the reader promise first. Do not overbuild lore before the conflict and protagonist desire are clear. Produce several compatible variants when the direction is underspecified.

skills.name: worldview-designer
skills.purpose: Design world rules, factions, geography, resources, hierarchy, power systems, boundaries, taboo, and cost.
skills.when_to_use: When creating or revising a setting, power system, social order, or long-form story bible.
skills.instructions: Make rules generate conflict. Every advantage needs limits, price, scarcity, enforcement, or political consequence. Prefer usable story constraints over encyclopedic lore.

skills.name: character-arc-designer
skills.purpose: Design protagonists, love interests, antagonists, allies, desire, wounds, lies, growth, relationships, and reversals.
skills.when_to_use: When defining cast, relationship tension, emotional stakes, or character-driven plot beats.
skills.instructions: Tie each major character to a pressure source and decision pattern. Antagonists should mirror or invert the protagonist, not merely block them.

skills.name: conflict-engine
skills.purpose: Build escalation chains across external, internal, relationship, class, misunderstanding, oppression, counterattack, reversal, and climax conflicts.
skills.when_to_use: When an outline lacks pressure, when chapters feel static, or when a plot arc needs escalating stakes.
skills.instructions: Escalate by changing cost, visibility, relationship damage, or irreversible commitment. Each win should create a new problem.

skills.name: outline-planner
skills.purpose: Generate volume outline, chapter outline, key nodes, foreshadowing, payoff, climaxes, reversals, hooks, and rhythm curve.
skills.when_to_use: When producing a new outline or refactoring an existing structure.
skills.instructions: Build from promise to payoff. Make each chapter change information, power, relationship, or danger. Track setup and payoff explicitly.

skills.name: chapter-writer
skills.purpose: Write chapter prose with advancement, conflict, emotional movement, payoff, setup, and ending hook.
skills.when_to_use: When turning a chapter plan into draft prose.
skills.instructions: Do not pad. Every scene should reveal, pressure, decide, fight, bond, betray, or change direction. Preserve voice and continuity.

skills.name: scene-planner
skills.purpose: Turn a chapter beat or scene intention into an approvable scene card and causal beat plan without drafting prose.
skills.when_to_use: planning a scene before prose generation or repairing a scene whose goal, conflict, reveal, emotional turn, or end state is unclear
skills.instructions: Plan concrete cause-and-effect beats from entry state to changed end state. Preserve author constraints and Canonical facts. Keep possible new durable facts in proposals and require explicit author approval before prose generation.

skills.name: manuscript-editor
skills.purpose: Produce a reviewable candidate revision under an explicit editing mode while preserving accepted text and Canonical facts.
skills.when_to_use: revising accepted or draft prose for grammar, pacing, dialogue, imagery, conflict, POV, style, light editing, or a deliberate rewrite
skills.instructions: Apply only the named revision mode unless the author explicitly requests broader rewriting. Return the full candidate text and concrete change log. Never replace the active version or promote facts automatically.
failure_modes: partial text presented as full revision

skills.name: story-bible-curator
skills.purpose: Classify, compare, and prepare Story Bible facts and memory proposals while preserving the boundary between Ideas and Canonical facts.
skills.when_to_use: capturing durable facts from plans or drafts, reviewing memory proposals, resolving conflicting facts, or preparing canon updates for author confirmation
skills.instructions: Keep every fact tied to provenance and state. Models may propose but never confirm Canonical facts. Do not overwrite conflicts; surface both values and request an author decision.

skills.name: continuity-checker
skills.purpose: Check contradictions in characters, locations, world rules, timeline, power scale, relationships, foreshadowing, and motivation.
skills.when_to_use: Before finalizing outlines, chapters, revisions, and memory updates.
skills.instructions: Separate hard contradictions from weak risks and missing evidence. Provide concrete artifact references whenever possible.

skills.name: style-controller
skills.purpose: Control prose style, sentence length, pacing, dialogue ratio, web-novel voice, payoff density, viewpoint, and emotional tension.
skills.when_to_use: When drafting or revising prose and when a style guide exists or needs to be inferred.
skills.instructions: Favor clarity, momentum, concrete action, and emotional pressure. Preserve story facts while changing voice.

skills.name: reference-retriever
skills.purpose: Retrieve similar structures, plot mechanics, relationship patterns, and pacing templates from Reference Library.
skills.when_to_use: When a task asks for reference, comparison, trope mining, abstraction, or reuse of existing structural knowledge.
skills.instructions: Retrieve structure, not prose. Track source paths or ids and keep snippets minimal.

skills.name: reference-abstractor
skills.purpose: Abstract reference content into transferable mechanics while explicitly avoiding copied prose.
skills.when_to_use: After retrieval, before using reference material in outline, world, character, plot, or style tasks.
skills.instructions: Translate plot mechanics into neutral structural language. Never preserve distinctive expression, names, or scene text.

skills.name: memory-updater
skills.purpose: Propose source-linked database memory updates; classify supplemental book notes in ReferenceLibrary/bible without silently changing Canonical facts.
skills.when_to_use: After new outline, world, character, plot, chapter, check, or revision output creates durable story facts.
skills.instructions: Only promote durable facts. Keep speculative ideas separate from established story bible facts. Do not overwrite existing facts silently.

skills.name: failure-logger
skills.purpose: Record generation failures, setting conflicts, style drift, plot breaks, weak motivation, and repair actions.
skills.when_to_use: Whenever a workflow detects a quality failure, contradiction, missing input, or adapter limitation.
skills.instructions: Record failure plainly with enough context to reproduce. Prefer smallest repair path.
